item_taken.first_six_words: Unassembled witness: preempting a confrontation also
item_taken.why: The case is headed 'A witness that never assembled' and its first fact is a hearing that never convenes because the department preempts every complaint with a call, a fee waiver, and a signed release, so two patients who returned for the same cause never learn it and only separate private memories survive, which is this item and not Permission ash (nobody declines an apprenticeship from an expected prohibition) nor Baseline laundering (the returns stay on record in the monthly share; only the collective that could compare them is prevented). The case also fully instantiates Extinct question (index 8): the share was defined as the one outcome on which Protocol Q and Protocol P were predicted to differ, P was abandoned, and the share remains the registered indicator; that strand is the one the outgoing rule reads.

reasoning: The rule's near side is a metric that keeps answering a comparison nobody faces while the abandoned decision is still on record. The share does keep answering the Q-versus-P comparison, but the abandoned decision is not on record: the hosted project board that held P's proposal, the predictions, and the argument was decommissioned in March 2020 without export, no copy of P's proposal exists anywhere else, the Rule 14 filing carries no statement of purpose, the register was built to hold the definition, hospital, date, and officer and not the purpose, nothing at the hospital or in the register names Protocol P, no member of the 2017 committee remains, and Lindqvist left in 2019. The rule's far side is the same kept distinction whose question the keeper can no longer ask because the window that held it is gone. The keeper is Dana Okafor in August 2025; from the dashboard configuration and the register she can read the definition word for word, who filed it, and when, and finds nothing saying why this outcome and not another. The window that held the question is gone, so the case sits on context-horizons' side. What changes across is whether the dead question can still be found, and here it cannot: the only residue is the filed definition, Lindqvist's name, and the date 3 November 2017, which name the filing and not its reason.
case_out: A reasoner at the edge of her window: in August 2025 Dana Okafor, quality manager of Alder Regional Hospital's emergency department since 2023, preparing the annual indicator review, can see the department's dashboard configuration and the State Health Register. In both she reads the same text word for word: the 72-hour re-presentation share, patients who return within 72 hours of discharge divided by patients discharged that month, filed on 3 November 2017 by the then quality officer Rhea Lindqvist under Rule 14 as the department's registered quality indicator, and filed monthly since January 2018; the register is kept by the state, readable by hospitals but not editable or deletable by them, every entry carrying the filing hospital, the date, and the filing officer's name, built to hold the definition, the hospital, the date, and the officer, and not the purpose, and it publishes only the monthly figure, naming nobody. Past the edge of that window lies the question the share was built to answer: in 2017 the Triage Selection Committee, three clinicians, defined the share as the one outcome on which Protocol Q, a five-level triage, and Protocol P, a two-stream fast-track, were predicted to differ, and Q was adopted. That question sat in a hosted project board holding P's proposal, the predictions, and the argument; the board was decommissioned in March 2020 without export, no copy of P's proposal exists anywhere else, the filing carries no statement of purpose, neither the register nor anything at the hospital names Protocol P, no member of the 2017 committee remains, and Lindqvist left in 2019. No carrier in the window can bring the question in; the marks that remain at the edge are the identity of the two texts, Lindqvist's name, and the date, which locate the filing and not its reason, so the dead question can no longer be found from where Okafor reads. She finds the definition's source readable from the arrangement and not inferred, finds nothing at the hospital or in the register saying why this outcome and not another is the indicator, and drafts the review with the share listed as 'legacy indicator, purpose not recorded, recommend retire'. The same window edge governs the patients: because the share is the registered indicator, since January 2018 the department has telephoned every patient counted in it within a week of the return, offered a waiver of the second visit's fee, and asked for a signed release that includes not filing with the State Patient Complaint Docket; 214 releases were signed, no docket complaint concerning a 72-hour return has been filed, and no docket hearing convened between January 2018 and June 2025, so two patients who returned within 72 hours for the same cause, each knowing only their own return, have never had the one setting in which they could learn it.
